title: KuSL2023: A standard for Kurdish sign language detection and classification using hand tracking and machine learning
author: Rawf

steps.title: Load source image datasets
steps.instruction: Load the ASL dataset containing RGB images for 11 Kurdish letters and the ArSL2018 dataset containing grayscale images for the remaining 23 Kurdish letters.

steps.title: Align letters and select images
steps.instruction: For each Kurdish alphabet letter, match it to the appropriate source dataset: if a similar shape exists in ASL, select exactly 3,000 RGB images (unaltered); otherwise, filter the corresponding grayscale images from ArSL2018, remove near‑duplicate samples, and retain between 1,290 and 3,000 images per class. Resize all selected images to a standard size of 64 × 64 pixels.

steps.title: Construct balanced dataset
steps.instruction: Create the KuSL2023 dataset containing a total of 71,400 images (34 classes). Ensure each RGB‑based class holds exactly 3,000 images (total 33,000 RGB images across 11 classes) and each grayscale class holds between 1,290 and 3,000 images (total 38,400 grayscale images across 23 classes). Store RGB images (≈3 MB per class) and grayscale images (≈10 KB per image) in their respective class folders.

steps.title: Preprocess data for each model type

substeps.instruction: For KNN and LightGBM (grayscale‑only): convert every image to grayscale, resize to 64 × 64, flatten to a 1‑D vector, normalize pixel values, encode class names with LabelEncoder, split the dataset into training and test sets using stratified sampling (80 % train / 20 % test), and scale features with StandardScaler.

For CNN (RGB): load images with tf.keras.image_dataset_from_directory using image_size=(64,64), batch_size=64, validation_split=0.1, color_mode='rgb'; rescale pixel values to [0,1]; define a CNN architecture comprising Conv2D, MaxPool, Dropout, and Dense layers; compile with the Adam optimizer and a softmax output layer.

steps.title: Train and evaluate models
steps.instruction: For each model (CNN, KNN, LightGBM): train on the training set, validate on the validation split if applicable, predict on the test set, and record runtime (CNN ≈ 6679 s, KNN ≈ 79.58 s, LightGBM ≈ 481.37 s). Compute performance metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1‑Score.

steps.title: Report model performance
steps.instruction: Report the following results: CNN – 98.22 % accuracy, 97.79 % precision, 97.73 % recall, 97.75 % F1; KNN – 95.98 % accuracy, 96.02 % precision, 95.98 % recall, 95.99 % F1; LightGBM – 96.94 % accuracy, 96.20 % precision, 96.15 % recall, 96.16 % F1.

steps.title: Visualize training and confusion matrix
steps.instruction: For the CNN model, plot training and validation accuracy and loss curves, and generate a confusion matrix to visualize class‑wise predictions.

steps.title: Compute evaluation equations
steps.instruction: Calculate metrics using: Accuracy = (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN); Precision = TP/(TP+FP); Recall = TP/(TP+FN); F1 = 2·TP/(2·TP+FP+FN).
